thread:
lara: FYI — customer ACME Mobile reporting OAuth callback failures from our hosted auth flow when their iOS app uses a custom scheme (acme://auth). They see the browser redirect back to the app but then our backend logs state_mismatch. They migrated to our new edge proxy last week and said it broke afterwards.

jordan: Did they paste any raw redirect URLs? state mismatch usually means the returned state string doesn't match session-stored value. Could be PKCE/state padding or encoding getting altered by the proxy.

lara: Yes — excerpt from their capture (redacted):

  acme://auth?code=abcd1234&state=Y3VzdG9tZXN0YXRlLWRvZXNuJw

They say the state used to end with '==' before migration.

sam: Interesting — base64 padding being stripped is a known pitfall. Some proxies or URL normalizers strip trailing '=' characters. If we store session state as the padded form but the client returns the unpadded form, verification fails.

nora: Ops note — our new edge-proxy has a query-normalize feature that canonicalizes query params and currently removes trailing '=' characters from values when safe_mode is on. I suspected this could affect base64-style tokens.

lara: Support repro steps we used:
1) Start OAuth authorize: GET https://auth.redwood.com/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=acme://auth&state=Rk9PQj0
2) Edge rewrites and proxies redirect to acme://auth?code=...&state=Rk9PQj
3) Our server receives callback and compares state_from_query (Rk9PQj) with state_in_session (Rk9PQj0==) -> mismatch -> 400

jordan: I ran a local test against the staging edge with a state of 'Rk9PQj0==' and saw it arrive at backend as 'Rk9PQj'. Repro confirmed.

sam: Two mitigation options:
- Short-term: server-side normalization: when verifying state, accept either padded or unpadded base64 by normalizing both sides (e.g., add padding until len%4==0).
- Mid-term: update edge config to preserve trailing padding for query values that look like base64.
- Long-term: switch to base64url (no padding) consistently across client and server, and update docs/SDKs.

jordan: Code snippet to normalize state (JS) I pasted into the thread for quick PR:

```js
function normalizeBase64State(s) {
  // convert url-safe -> standard, then pad to multiple of 4
  s = s.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
  while (s.length % 4 !== 0) s += '=';
  return s;
}

// example usage
if (normalizeBase64State(receivedState) !== normalizeBase64State(sessionState)) {
  throw new Error('state_mismatch');
}
```

nora: I'm going to flip the edge flag to stop stripping trailing '=' for a minute in staging to confirm the fix. If that fixes, we'll do a one-line hotfix to preserve padding.

lara: Customer workaround while we roll: ask their iOS team to URL-encode the state and ensure their custom scheme handler preserves query params. But since the proxy is at our edge, this is fragile — better to fix here.

sam: Note for DevEx/SDKs: we should document this behaviour and add a normalization helper in our mobile SDK so apps sending states are tolerant. Also a short issue about switching to base64url without padding to avoid '=' entirely.

ops-bot: rollout/start — edge-proxy config change staging started by nora at 2026-03-14T18:20:00Z

nora: Staging test passed: state arrived padded and backend accepted it. I'll schedule prod flip after 30m smoke.

lara: Great — I'll update ACME support ticket with root cause = edge query normalization removed base64 padding, and steps we took. Also included suggested SDK normalization snippet.

jordan: After prod flip we should add a lightweight regression test in our auth e2e to generate padded state and ensure it survives the full redirect chain.

lara: Agreed. Closing loop after prod deploy. :thumbsup:
